symptom.duration: Skin findings (café-au-lait spots, axillary freckling) first noted in late teens; cutaneous neurofibromas and dome-shaped soft nodules gradually developed over the past 20 years. Spinal pain and sensory abnormalities have been intermittent for 8-10 years, with mild memory impairment and pigmentation deepening becoming apparent over the last 2 years. Symptoms have progressed slowly without acute exacerbations.

examination_results.Genetic Testing: Sequencing of the NF1 gene identified a pathogenic heterozygous nonsense mutation at exon 21, c.2345C>T (p.Arg782*), with a variant allele frequency of 48%. No large deletions or duplications detected. Family testing confirms paternal inheritance.
examination_results.Ultrasound Examination: Multiple well-defined, hypoechoic masses are visualized in the subcutaneous tissue of the posterior thoracic and lumbar regions, the largest measuring 1.9 x 1.6 cm. No vascularity within nodules on Doppler. No abnormal findings in abdominal or pelvic cavity on survey.
examination_results.X-ray Examination: AP and lateral views reveal mild right convex scoliosis with a Cobb angle of 14 degrees. Curvilinear radiolucent streaks noted adjacent to the L2 and L3 vertebral bodies, consistent with extrinsic soft tissue masses. No obvious bony erosion, fractures, or long bone deformities observed.
examination_results.Ophthalmic Examination: Slit lamp evaluation demonstrates multiple raised, well-circumscribed yellow-brown nodules (1–2 mm diameter) on both irides, consistent with iris hamartomas; 6 nodules on right, 4 on left. No optic disc edema, pallor, or evidence of optic atrophy. Visual acuity OD 20/20, OS 20/25.
examination_results.CTM Test: Post-contrast thoracolumbar spinal CT reveals two low-density masses at the left paraspinal region, largest measuring 2.1 x 1.4 cm, with CT attenuation values of 24 HU. Mild cortical erosion noted at posterior aspect of L2 vertebral body. No evidence of intraspinal extension.
examination_results.MRI Examination: T1-weighted imaging demonstrates iso- to mildly hyperintense masses in paraspinal soft tissues, largest is 2.3 x 1.7 cm. T2-weighted images show heterogeneously hyperintense lesions with central areas of slightly lower signal in 58% of tumor cross-section, suggestive of fibrous stroma. Mild left lateral displacement of nerve roots at L2–L3 with no evidence of significant cord compression.
examination_results.Spinal Angiography: Contrast injection visualizes distinct filling defects at the proximal left L3 nerve root, correlating with known mass location. No abnormal vascularity or large feeding vessels identified. Procedure complicated by minor reflux into soft tissue, confirming mass continuity with nerve root structure. No signs of arteriovenous malformation.

Intermittent spinal pain over past decade
Mild memory impairment noted by family over last 2 years
Annual skin checks revealing gradual increase in cutaneous neurofibromas
No prior history of optic glioma or significant vision loss

name: Edward Harrington

symptom.duration: Many symptoms have been present since adolescence, with slow but progressive worsening over decades. In the last 10 years, neurological complications (including memory impairment, seizures, optic glioma with complete vision loss in the right eye, and spinal pain due to worsening scoliosis and bone destruction) have become significantly more severe, with noticeable deterioration in the past 2-3 years.

examination_results.Genetic Testing: Sequencing of peripheral blood DNA reveals a heterozygous, pathogenic nonsense mutation in exon 31 of the NF1 gene (c.4537C>T, p.Arg1513*), with loss-of-function confirmed. No additional significant mutations detected in NF2, TSC1, or TSC2. Variant allele frequency: 49%. Family pedigree analysis supports autosomal dominant inheritance.
examination_results.Ultrasound Examination: High-frequency probe of the skin and subcutaneous tissues identifies multiple, heterogenous, hypoechoic solid masses ranging from 1.2 cm to 6.4 cm in diameter, with poorly defined borders and posterior acoustic enhancement; some deep masses in axilla and lower abdomen measuring up to 8.7 cm. Vascularity within lesions is mild to moderate on Doppler. No cystic degeneration or calcification seen.
examination_results.X-ray Examination: AP and lateral radiographs of thoracolumbar spine reveal marked right-sided convex scoliosis (Cobb angle 55°). Irregular cortical erosion and expansion is noted in vertebral bodies T9-L3, with elongated linear lucencies extending 2-4 cm suggestive of intramedullary growths. Multiple areas of widened neural foramina and thinning of long bones in left femur and humerus are observed. No acute fractures. Signs of diffuse osteopenia are present.
examination_results.Ophthalmic Examination: Slit lamp exam of left eye reveals more than 8 distinct, raised, light brown-yellow nodules (Lisch nodules) measuring 0.5-1.5 mm on iris surface; no similar findings in right eye, which shows optic disc pallor and severe atrophy. Visual acuity: left eye 0.2 (20/100), right eye no light perception. Mild conjunctival injection present in left eye. No signs of increased intraocular pressure.
examination_results.CTM Test: Contrast-enhanced CT of thoracolumbar spine and pelvis reveals multiple lobulated, low-density soft tissue masses (mean CT value 22 HU) encasing nerve roots and extending into paraspinal regions. Marked vertebral erosion noted at T10, L1, and L3, with up to 40% loss of vertebral height. Contrast medium surrounds masses, delineating margins distinctly. Neural foramina of L2-L4 are expanded >6 mm bilaterally.
examination_results.MRI Examination: Axial and sagittal T1-weighted images show multiple paraspinal and cutaneous masses with isointense to mildly hyperintense signal (similar to adjacent muscle), largest measuring 9.2 x 5.6 cm at L2. T2-weighted sequences reveal these lesions as mixed hyperintense with central areas of slightly lower signal in approximately 60% of tumours. Severe right optic nerve enlargement with marked gliosis, as well as diffuse, irregular thickening of skin in thoracic region. Brain MRI notes mild diffuse cerebral atrophy and scattered white matter hyperintensities.
examination_results.Spinal Angiography: Digital subtraction angiography of lumbar and sacral spine demonstrates multiple contrast defects at nerve root exit zones of L1-L4. When contrast medium is injected into the region of the largest paraspinal mass (L2 level), rapid filling of tumour vascular channels is seen, confirming intralesional presence. Mild arteriovenous shunting observed around plexiform mass, no major vessel compromise.

Progressive cutaneous and plexiform neurofibromas since teens
Surgical removal of neurofibromas on multiple occasions
History of scoliosis since adolescence, progressively worsening

Intermittent epileptic seizures over past decade
Mild memory impairment diagnosed at age 85

name: Helen Cartwright

examination_results.Genetic Testing: Targeted sequencing of the NF1 gene identified a heterozygous pathogenic frameshift mutation in exon 31 (c.3721_3722del; p.Leu1241Valfs*2), consistent with an inherited abnormality. No additional pathogenic variants detected in NF2 or SPRED1. Variant interpretation is consistent with her family history.
examination_results.Ultrasound Examination: Multiple well-circumscribed, hypoechoic soft tissue nodules are visualized in the subcutaneous plane of the posterior thorax, with the largest measuring 2.8 x 1.9 x 1.3 cm. No internal vascularity or calcification noted. A solitary, oval-shaped hypoechoic lesion (1.2 cm diameter) is visualized in the left lower abdominal wall. No findings of intra-abdominal organ involvement.
examination_results.X-ray Examination: Thoracolumbar spine radiograph reveals rightward curvature consistent with scoliosis (Cobb angle 19°), mild vertebral scalloping at L3-L4, and foci of cortical thinning along the right femur shaft. No pathological fractures or lytic lesions observed. Several elongated, radiolucent bands (up to 2.5 cm) are seen adjacent to vertebral pedicles, suggestive of osseous neurofibromatous lesions.
examination_results.Ophthalmic Examination: Slit lamp evaluation reveals multiple (6 per eye) raised, well-circumscribed, yellow-brown nodules ranging from 1 to 2 mm in diameter on the iris consistent with hamartomatous changes. Optic discs with sharp margins and no pallor or papilledema. Visual acuity: OD 20/20, OS 20/25. No evidence of optic pathway glioma or lenticular opacities.
examination_results.CTM Test: Contrast-enhanced CT myelogram demonstrates a 2.4 x 1.7 cm oval mass at the right L4 neural exit foramen; the lesion is surrounded by contrast medium and displays a core low density (CT value: 25 HU). Associated mild cortical bone erosion at the adjacent pedicle is observed. No intradural extension visualized. Other spinal regions show no additional mass effect.
examination_results.MRI Examination: Sagittal and axial T1-weighted images reveal multiple well-defined paraspinal and subcutaneous lesions measuring up to 3.0 cm; lesions exhibit isointense to mildly hyperintense signal relative to muscle. On T2-weighted images, these lesions are markedly hyperintense with areas of slightly lower central intensity in approximately 60% of the larger nodules, reflecting fibrous composition. No evidence of malignant transformation or spinal cord compression.
examination_results.Spinal Angiography: Digital subtraction angiography shows contrast medium displacement and a clear filling defect at right L4-L5 spinal nerve root exit, with impaired venous outflow. Contrast extravasation is absent. During angiography, inadvertent contrast pooling occurs within the 2.4 cm mass correlating with prior neuroimaging, confirming its presence and vascular relationship.

name: Emily Harrison

symptoms: Dome-shaped soft nodules over trunk and limbs
symptom.duration: Café-au-lait spots and freckling appeared in early childhood; cutaneous neurofibromas became prominent and increased in size and number through adolescence and adulthood, with rapid progression over the past year. Neurological symptoms, including seizures and memory impairment, have worsened in the past 2–3 years. Spinal pain and skeletal deformities, such as scoliosis and kyphosis, have progressively intensified since the teenage years. Recent onset of orbital skin mass and worsening proptosis over six months.

examination_results.Genetic Testing: Next-generation sequencing of peripheral blood DNA shows a heterozygous pathogenic nonsense mutation in exon 17 of the NF1 gene (c.2041C>T, p.Arg681Ter) with a variant allele frequency of 49%. No large deletions detected in NF2 gene. Parental testing confirms maternal inheritance of the NF1 mutation.
examination_results.Ultrasound Examination: High-frequency ultrasound of the trunk reveals over 15 well-defined, hypoechoic masses ranging from 0.9 cm to 3.2 cm in diameter, predominantly subcutaneous. Doppler imaging shows mild vascularization of the largest nodules. An abdominal scan identifies a 2.5 cm solid mass adjacent to the left paraspinal region, without involvement of intra-abdominal organs.
examination_results.X-ray Examination: Thoracolumbar X-rays demonstrate a left-sided scoliotic curvature with Cobb angle measuring 38 degrees and associated mild kyphosis. Multiple fusiform radiolucencies, consistent with neurofibroma involvement, are noted along the neural foramina at T8-T12. No bony destruction but cortical thinning observed in the lower thoracic vertebrae.
examination_results.Ophthalmic Examination: Slit lamp reveals the presence of 6 dome-shaped, brown-yellow raised nodules on the iris of the right eye and 5 on the left (average size 1-2 mm), consistent with iris hamartomas. Fundus exam shows pale, blurred margins of the right optic disc (cup-disc ratio 0.2) with mild disc elevation. Visual acuity is decreased: right eye 0.4, left eye 0.7. Moderate proptosis (4 mm forward displacement) of the right eye; an orbital cutaneous mass (2.3 cm) is palpable adjacent to the upper lid.
examination_results.CTM Test: Contrast-enhanced CT of the cervicothoracic spine reveals an irregular, low-density mass (CT value 24 HU) encasing the right T9 nerve root, measuring 2.8 x 1.5 cm. Additional low-density subcutaneous masses noted over posterior lumbar region (CT value 22-28 HU).
examination_results.MRI Examination: MRI of the spine and orbit shows a 2.7 cm paraspinal mass at T9 with uniform isointense signal on T1 (comparable to adjacent muscle, SI = 510) and high, heterogeneous signal on T2 (SI = 1170), with central area of mildly hypointense signal (SI = 525) corresponding to fibrous content. Multiple cutaneous nodules evident over lumbar region (size 0.8–2.0 cm), all hyperintense on T2-weighted images. Right orbital region shows a 2.5 cm mass compressing the globe and stretching extraocular muscles.
examination_results.Spinal Angiography: Digital subtraction angiography of lumbar spine reveals contrast staining defects adjacent to the exiting right L3 nerve root, with segmental filling delay and slight compression of local venous plexuses. During injection, accidental pooling of contrast within a 2.2 cm soft tissue mass at L3-L4 confirms intra-tumoral location. No overt arteriovenous malformation detected; moderate displacement of adjacent vascular anatomy.

examination_results.X-ray Examination: Spinal X-ray shows right-sided thoracolumbar scoliosis with a Cobb angle of 28°. Multiple vertebral scalloping observed at T8–L1. examination_results.Spinal Angiography: Digital subtraction angiography reveals contrast flow interruption at the right L4 nerve root exit, measuring approximately 2.2 cm in diameter. name: Liang Wei Chen

Urinalysis reveals leukocytes (++), nitrate positive, consistent with recent urinary infection.
examination_results.Imaging Tests: Brain MRI (1.5T): Mild generalized cortical and subcortical atrophy, bilateral frontal and temporal regions, with moderate periventricular white matter hyperintensities (Fazekas grade 2). No acute infarct or hemorrhage. Midbrain shows subtle flattening of the superior colliculus with decreased size of substantia nigra, left greater than right. PET (FDG): Reduced uptake in bilateral basal ganglia and thalamus, with decreased metabolism also noted in the posterior temporal and parietal lobes. SPECT (DAT scan): Markedly reduced striatal tracer uptake, especially in the putamen (>75% reduction compared to age-matched control values).
examination_results.Sniff Stick Test: Score: 3 out of 12 (normal: ≥10/12), indicating severe hyposmia. Patient unable to correctly identify common odors including coffee, banana, or rose. Subjective reporting of noticeable loss of smell sensation over the last several years.
examination_results.Transcranial Ultrasound: Transcranial sonography reveals bilateral hyperechogenicity of the substantia nigra, maximum area measured at 0.33 cm² on the right and 0.30 cm² on the left (normal <0.20 cm²). Cardiac 123I-MIBG scintigraphy demonstrates reduced heart-to-mediastinum (H/M) ratio: Early phase = 1.28 (reference ≥1.8), delayed phase = 1.07 (reference ≥1.6), with increased washout rate. Findings consistent with marked cardiac sympathetic denervation.

symptom.duration: Initial subtle symptoms (constipation, reduced sense of smell) started approximately 2 years ago; mild resting tremor and bradykinesia noticed in the past 8 months with gradual progression. Symptoms remain mild and do not interfere significantly with daily activities.

examination_results.Laboratory Tests: Cerebrospinal fluid analysis shows homovanillic acid (HVA) level at 80 nmol/L (reference: 110–280 nmol/L), mildly reduced. No significant abnormalities in routine labs.
examination_results.Imaging Tests: Brain MRI reveals normal brain parenchyma without evidence of vascular lesions, mass, or atrophy. No diffusion restriction or abnormal enhancement. Dopaminergic SPECT scan (e.g., DaTscan) shows mild asymmetrical decreased uptake in the left striatum (striatum: right 2.1; left 1.6; mean normal range: 2.5-3.0), with preserved cortical uptake.
examination_results.Sniff Stick Test: Patient identifies 7 out of 12 scents correctly (reference: ≥10 correct in healthy older adults), indicating reduced olfactory identification ability. Notably incorrect on odors such as peppermint and banana.
examination_results.Transcranial Ultrasound: Substantia nigra hyperechogenicity noted on right side with an area of 0.24 cm² (normal <0.20 cm²), left side within normal limits. Cardiac MIBG scintigraphy demonstrates early heart-to-mediastinum (H/M) ratio of 1.77 (normal >2.0), indicating mild reduction in myocardial uptake. No other focal abnormalities.

family_history: no known family history of Parkinson's disease

symptoms: resting tremor (more pronounced in both hands)

Non-motor symptoms like constipation and reduced sense of smell began about 7 years ago, predating motor changes. Cognitive changes and low mood developed over the last 2 years. examination_results.Laboratory Tests: Cerebrospinal fluid analysis shows homovanillic acid (HVA) level at 22.5 ng/mL (reference range: 35–70 ng/mL), indicating a significant decrease. Other parameters, including cell count, protein (38 mg/dL), and glucose (64 mg/dL), are within normal limits. No evidence of infection or inflammation noted.
examination_results.Imaging Tests: PET scan reveals bilateral reduction in striatal fluorodopa uptake, more pronounced in the posterior putamen (right: 30% of normal, left: 32% of normal). SPECT (DaT scan) shows asymmetric decrease in dopamine transporter binding, with specific binding ratios of 1.1 (right) and 1.0 (left) compared to reference >2.0. MRI brain displays age-related atrophy, mild ventricular enlargement, and no acute lesions or mass effect.
examination_results.Sniff Stick Test: Patient identifies 4 out of 12 test odors correctly (normal ≥10), consistent with marked impairment in olfactory discrimination. Responses are delayed and olfactory threshold appears elevated.
examination_results.Transcranial Ultrasound: Substantia nigra echogenic area measured at 0.23 cm² (reference <0.20 cm²); this area is hyperechogenic bilaterally. Cardiac MIBG scintigraphy reveals heart-to-mediastinum (H/M) ratio of 1.32 in the early phase and 1.16 in delayed imaging (normal >1.6), suggesting reduced uptake. No evidence of vascular malformations or hemorrhage.

Fatigue and myalgia developed on the second day; loss of appetite noticed since yesterday. No progression to severe symptoms or neurological deficits; all symptoms have remained mild and stable.

examination_results.Physical Examination: Temperature: 38.2°C (oral). Pulse: 85 bpm, regular. Blood pressure: 128/80 mmHg. Respiratory rate: 18/min. General appearance: alert and oriented, appears mildly fatigued. No skin rash. Neck: mild nuchal rigidity noted on passive flexion, but able to touch chin to chest with mild discomfort. Kernig’s and Brudzinski’s signs negative. Cranial nerves: II-XII intact. No focal motor or sensory deficits. Gait normal. No photic-induced eye movements. No signs of papilledema on fundoscopic examination.
examination_results.Laboratory Tests: CBC: WBC 8.7 x10^9/L (reference: 4-10); neutrophils 52%, lymphocytes 39%, monocytes 7%. Hemoglobin 14.1 g/dL, platelets 210 x10^9/L. CRP 6 mg/L (reference: <5). Serum electrolytes, renal and liver function normal. Blood culture negative at 48 hours. Nasopharyngeal swab PCR: enterovirus negative, HSV-1/2 negative, VZV negative. Throat swab PCR: negative. No significant elevation of procalcitonin.
examination_results.Imaging Tests: Non-contrast cranial CT: no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, or hydrocephalus. No abnormal hypo- or hyperdensities seen. Contrast-enhanced MRI (if performed): no meningeal enhancement, no parenchymal lesions. No abnormal signal in the parenchyma or ventricles. EEG not performed due to absence of seizure or encephalopathic features.
examination_results.Lumbar puncture and cerebrospinal fluid: Opening pressure: 18 cm H2O (normal: 10-20 cm H2O). CSF appearance: clear, colorless. WBC 124 x10^6/L (predominantly lymphocytes: 82%, monocytes: 14%, neutrophils: 4%). CSF protein: 0.52 g/L (normal: 0.15–0.45 g/L). CSF glucose: 3.7 mmol/L (serum glucose 5.5 mmol/L; CSF/Serum ratio ~0.67, normal). CSF chloride: 122 mmol/L (normal: 118–130 mmol/L). Gram stain: no organisms seen. CSF bacterial and fungal cultures: negative at 48 hours. CSF viral PCR panel: enterovirus, HSV-1/2, VZV, mumps, CMV all negative.

name: Amina Ndlovu
